speaker: Connor McGarr (Origin/Prelude Security)
theme: Discovers and abuses an undocumented WMI_LOGGER_CONTEXT.Flags.SecurityTrace bit (bit 14) protecting Defender's DefenderApiLogger/DefenderAuditLogger AutoLogger ETW sessions; shows a path to consuming Microsoft-Windows-Threat-Intelligence ETW events without Antimalware-PPL or a kernel driver; releases ThreatIntelligenceConsumer PoC

title: CVE-2024-21423 — Microsoft Edge Prefs Enclave TOCTOU (Information Disclosure + VTL1 Write Primitive)
speaker: Alex Gough (quidity), Google Project Zero
theme: TOCTOU race in Edge's prefs_enclave_x64.dll SealSettings/UnsealSettings allows arbitrary read/write in VTL1 enclave memory due to user-supplied pointers not being copied before crossing the VTL0→VTL1 trust boundary

title: Abusing VBS Enclaves to Create Evasive Malware
speaker: Ori David, Akamai
theme: PoC weaponizing the Microsoft Edge prefs enclave for sleep masking: shellcode is sealed into VTL1 via SealSettings during sleep, making it invisible to VTL0 kernel-mode inspection (EDR drivers) while the implant is dormant

title: Forest Compromise Through AMA (Authentication Mechanism Assurance) Abuse
speaker: Carl Sörqvist
theme: Groups configured with Authentication Mechanism Assurance (AMA) are implicitly trusted when any CA issues a certificate mapped to those groups; a compromised CA not in NTAuthCertificates can still compromise AMA groups if the certificate chain is trusted at a different level

title: DriverJack: Turning NTFS and Emulated Read-only Filesystems in an Infection and Persistence Vector
speaker: Alessandro Magnosi
theme: Abuses NTFS filesystem structures and read-only emulated virtual disk mounts as novel vectors to load unsigned drivers and persist malware across Windows reboots while evading driver signature enforcement
category: defense-evasion (driver loading / BYOVD-adjacent via NTFS manipulation)

title: Techniques for Creating Process Injection Attacks with Advanced Return-Oriented Programming
speaker: Bramwell Brizendine; Shiva Shashank Kusuma
theme: Presents a new method for Windows process injection using advanced ROP chains, bypassing DEP/CFG mitigations without shellcode by composing gadgets from Windows system DLLs

title: Abusing Windows Hello Without a Severed Hand
speaker: Ceri Coburn; Dirk-jan Mollema (dirkjanm)
theme: Demonstrates attacks against Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) that allow stealing/forging authentication tokens from enrolled devices without any physical biometric interaction, using the "Shwmae" toolset
category: credentials (Windows Hello for Business / PKINIT / certificate-based auth)

title: MaLDAPtive: LDAP Obfuscation, Deobfuscation, and Detection
speaker: Daniel Bohannon; Sabajete Elezaj
theme: Introduces an LDAP-based obfuscation and deobfuscation framework for Active Directory queries, showing how attackers can encode LDAP searches to evade EDR/SIEM detection, and builds a corresponding detection framework
category: AD-attack (LDAP obfuscation for Active Directory reconnaissance evasion)

title: HookChain: A new perspective for Bypassing EDR Solutions
speaker: Helvio Carvalho Junior
theme: Presents a new Windows syscall hooking chain that dynamically redirects execution through alternative NTDLL paths to bypass user-mode EDR hooks without triggering standard in-memory detections

title: NTLM: The Last Ride
speaker: Jim Rush; Tomais Williamson
theme: A comprehensive audit of Windows NTLM authentication's remaining attack surface as Microsoft moves toward NTLM deprecation, demonstrating still-exploitable relay, coercion, and authentication downgrade techniques

title: Outlook Unleashing RCE Chaos: CVE-2024-30103 & CVE-2024-38021
speaker: Michael Gorelik (Morphisec); Arnold Osipov (Morphisec)
theme: Demonstrates zero-click (CVE-2024-38021) and one-click (CVE-2024-30103) remote code execution vulnerabilities in Microsoft Outlook leveraging DLL side-loading from malicious email-triggered UNC paths
category: malware-analysis (Windows Outlook RCE via DLL side-load / COM hijack)

title: Sudos and Sudon'ts: Peering inside Sudo for Windows
speaker: Michael Torres (Microsoft)
theme: Analyzes Microsoft's new Sudo for Windows feature (shipped in Windows 11 24H2), dissecting its privilege boundary model, IPC implementation, and security implications for both administrators and attackers

title: SHIM me what you got: Manipulating Shim and Office for Code Injection
speaker: Ron Ben-Yizhak (Deep Instinct); David Shandalov (Deep Instinct)
theme: Explores abusing Windows Application Compatibility Shims and Microsoft Office COM objects as a code injection and persistence vector that survives reboots and evades most EDRs without requiring admin privileges
category: defense-evasion (Windows Shim Database / COM-based code injection)

title: Defeating magic by magic: Using ALPC security features to compromise RPC services
speaker: WangJunJie Zhang; YiSheng He
theme: Demonstrates a novel exploitation class against Windows ALPC (Advanced Local Procedure Call) where security features in the ALPC kernel implementation itself are twisted into a privilege escalation vector against RPC-based services

title: Defeating EDR-Evading Malware with Memory Forensics
speaker: Andrew Case; Austin Sellers; Golden Richard III; David McDonald; Gustavo Moreira
theme: Presents memory forensics techniques that detect advanced Windows EDR-evading malware (process hollowing, module stomping, heap-only shellcode) that bypass all telemetry-based EDR approaches, using the Volatility3 framework
category: malware-analysis (Windows memory forensics for EDR-evasion detection)

title: QuickShell: Sharing is caring about an RCE attack chain on Quick Share
speaker: Or Yair (SafeBreach); Shmuel Cohen (SafeBreach)
theme: Chains ten CVEs in Google's Quick Share (Windows Nearby Sharing equivalent) into a zero-interaction remote code execution exploit, fully weaponizing Windows peer-to-peer file transfer from across a network
category: post-exploitation (Windows app-layer RCE via peer-to-peer file sharing)

title: Where's the Money: Defeating ATM Disk Encryption
speaker: Matt Burch (Optiv)
theme: Demonstrates practical physical and software attacks against Windows-based ATM disk encryption configurations (BitLocker and third-party equivalents), enabling cold-boot and offline credential extraction from bank machines

title: Kill Chain Reloaded: Abusing legacy paths for stealth persistence
speaker: Alejandro Hernando; Borja Martinez
theme: Identifies multiple overlooked Windows legacy filesystem paths, COM registration entries, and service control paths that enable long-lived, stealthy persistence invisible to modern EDR behavioral monitoring

title: Infecting the Boot to Own the Kernel: Bootkits and Rootkits Development
speaker: Alejandro Vazquez Vazquez; Maria San Jose
theme: A deep technical walkthrough of building modern Windows UEFI bootkits and kernel rootkits from scratch, demonstrating pre-boot code execution chains that survive OS reinstall and bypass Secure Boot with vulnerable UEFI modules

title: OverLAPS: Overriding LAPS Logic
speaker: Antoine Goichot
theme: Discovers multiple logic flaws in Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) — both legacy and Microsoft LAPS — allowing low-privileged domain users to force LAPS password resets, enumerate credentials, and persist via registry manipulation
category: credentials (Windows LAPS abuse / Active Directory credential control)

title: Advanced Active Directory to Entra ID lateral movement techniques
speaker: Dirk-jan Mollema (dirkjanm / Outsider Security)
theme: Presents novel lateral movement paths from on-premises Active Directory into Entra ID (Azure AD) cloud using hybrid join trust relationships, Primary Refresh Token (PRT) manipulation, and Graph API abuse techniques
category: cloud-identity (AD-to-Entra lateral movement / hybrid identity attacks)

title: Can't Stop the ROP: Automating Universal ASLR Bypasses for Windows
speaker: Dr. Bramwell Brizendine
theme: Introduces automated tooling to discover universal ROP gadget chains that bypass ASLR across all Windows x64 system images at once, making previously impractical exploits programmatically buildable at scale
category: kernel-exploitation (Windows ASLR bypass automation via universal ROP)

title: What is Dead May Never Die: The Ghost of Internet Explorer in Windows MapUrlToZone
speaker: George Hughey; Rohit Mothe
theme: Reveals that IE-era URL zone mapping logic (MapUrlToZone) persists in Windows 11 and is actively used by Defender, Outlook, and Shell components, with exploitable zone-confusion flaws enabling Mark-of-the-Web / Protected View bypasses
category: defense-evasion (Windows MotW/Protected View bypass via legacy IE zone logic)

title: Turning Microsoft's Login Page into our Phishing Infrastructure
speaker: Keanu Nys
theme: Demonstrates how Microsoft's own login.microsoftonline.com and federation infrastructure can be co-opted as a transparent phishing proxy through OAuth redirect abuse, federation misconfiguration, and Pass-Through Authentication (PTA) token capture
category: cloud-identity (Microsoft Entra ID / OAuth phishing infrastructure abuse)

title: SCCM: The tree that always bears bad fruits
speaker: Mehdi Elyassa
theme: Uncovers new exploitation techniques against Microsoft System Center Configuration Manager (SCCM/ConfigMgr), enabling domain privilege escalation, lateral movement to other SCCM-managed hosts, and credential extraction from SCCM distribution points
category: AD-attack (Microsoft SCCM exploitation for domain privilege escalation)

title: ChromeAlone: Transforming a Browser into a C2 Platform
speaker: Michael "bouncyhat" Weber
theme: Demonstrates a novel Windows post-exploitation C2 technique using Chrome's remote debugging interface and DevTools Protocol to exfiltrate data, execute scripts, and maintain persistence from within a trusted browser process — evading EDR process-injection detections entirely
category: browser-windows-integration (Chrome DevTools Protocol as C2 on Windows)

title: Win-DoS Epidemic: A crash course in abusing RPC for Win-DoS & Win-DDoS
speaker: Or Yair (SafeBreach); Shahak Morag (SafeBreach)
theme: Systematically maps Windows RPC service attack surface to trigger non-paged-pool exhaustion and kernel handle table overflow conditions, producing unauthenticated local and network-sourced Windows denial-of-service from standard user accounts
category: other (Windows RPC-based DoS / kernel resource exhaustion)

title: Virtualization Based (In)Security
speaker: Ori David (Akamai)
theme: Audits Windows Virtualization-Based Security (VBS / HVCI) to reveal that features designed to protect Credential Guard and LSA secrets can be subverted from normal kernel mode, and that VBS-protected regions have exploitable side-channels

title: Turning your Active Directory into the attacker's C2: modern Group Policy Objects enumeration and exploitation
speaker: Quentin Roland; Wilfried Bécard
theme: Demonstrates how Group Policy Object (GPO) link hierarchy and delegation can be enumerated and abused to deploy attacker-controlled scripts and configurations across entire Active Directory organizational units without Domain Admin privileges
category: AD-attack (Group Policy Objects as lateral movement / persistence vectors)

title: You snooze you lose: RPC-Racer — winning RPC endpoints against services
speaker: Ron Ben Yizhak (Deep Instinct)
theme: Discovers a class of Windows TOCTOU (time-of-check/time-of-use) race conditions in high-privileged RPC server endpoints, enabling a low-privileged attacker to win races against SYSTEM-level services and escalate privileges by registering RPC endpoints between service start phases
category: kernel-exploitation (Windows RPC TOCTOU race for privilege escalation)

title: Original Sin of SSO: macOS PRT Cookie Theft & Entra ID Persistence via Device Forgery
speaker: Shang-De Jiang ("Kazma"); Dong-Yi Ye; Tung-Lin Lee ("Echo")
theme: Demonstrates that Primary Refresh Tokens (PRTs) — a core Windows-and-macOS SSO mechanism for Entra ID — can be stolen from macOS Enterprise SSO, then forged to register fake Entra ID-joined devices, enabling persistent cloud identity control that survives password reset
category: cloud-identity (Entra ID PRT theft / hybrid device trust bypass)

title: Mind the Data Voids: Hijacking Copilot Trust to Deliver C2 Instructions with Microsoft Authority
speaker: Tobias Diehl
theme: Exploits Microsoft Copilot's search grounding and SharePoint/Teams data retrieval to inject attacker-controlled C2 instructions into Copilot responses with apparent Microsoft authority, creating a prompt-injection C2 channel inside M365 tenants
category: cloud-identity (Microsoft Copilot/M365 prompt injection for C2)

title: The (Un)Rightful Heir: My dMSA Is Your New Domain Admin
speaker: Yuval Gordon
theme: Demonstrates a novel Active Directory attack abusing Delegated Managed Service Accounts (dMSA) — a Windows Server 2025 feature — to grant a low-privileged account implicit Domain Admin rights via linked principal chaining that bypasses standard ACL auditing
category: AD-attack (Windows Server 2025 dMSA delegation abuse to Domain Admin)

title: Ghosts in the Machine Check: Conjuring Hardware Failures for Cross-ring Privilege Escalation
speaker: Christopher Domas
theme: Discovers that Intel Machine Check Architecture (MCA) exceptions — normally hardware fault signals — can be synthetically triggered from Ring 3, causing the Windows kernel's Machine Check Handler to execute attacker-influenced data paths and enabling Ring 3-to-Ring 0 privilege escalation
category: hardware-attack (Intel MCA / cross-ring privilege escalation on Windows)

title: 7 Vulns in 7 Days: Breaking Bloatware Faster Than It's Built
speaker: Leon "leonjza" Jacobs
theme: Documents seven separate remotely-/locally-exploitable vulnerabilities found in one week across Windows OEM bloatware and driver-companion applications shipped pre-installed on major laptop brands, demonstrating systemic supply-chain quality failures
category: supply-chain (Windows OEM bloatware / pre-installed software vulnerabilities)

title: Ghost Calls: Abusing Web Conferencing for Covert Command & Control
speaker: Adam Crosser
theme: Demonstrates using Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Webex meeting APIs as a covert C2 channel running entirely inside trusted corporate processes on Windows, bypassing DLP, firewall inspection, and EDR network telemetry
category: post-exploitation (Teams/conferencing apps as Windows C2 channel)

title: Evading Modern Defenses When Phishing with Pixels
speaker: Melvin Langvik
theme: Demonstrates pixel-level steganographic and SVG-based phishing lure techniques that evade Windows Defender SmartScreen, Office Safe Links scanning, and email gateway attachment inspection

title: Countering Forensics Software by Baiting Them
speaker: Weihan Goh; Joseph Lim; Isaac Soon
theme: Presents anti-forensics techniques targeting Windows digital forensics tools (Autopsy, Volatility, FTK) by crafting deliberately malicious forensic artifacts — corrupt MFT entries, weaponized registry hives, and tainted memory images — that crash or mislead the analyst's tools

title: 10 Years of Windows Privilege Escalation with "Potatoes"
speaker: Andrea Pierini
theme: A decade-spanning tour of DCOM-based NTLM reflection and Cross-Session Activation exploits — RoguePotato through LocalPotato (CVE-2023-21746), SilverPotato, and the still-under-MSRC-review FakePotato — showing how Microsoft's refusal to treat WSH as a security boundary sustains the entire class

title: A Decade of Active Directory Attacks: What We've Learned & What's Next
speaker: Sean Metcalf
theme: Retrospective on the most effective AD and Azure AD/Entra ID attacks of 2014–2024 — Golden Ticket through modern cloud coercion — and how few organisations have actually closed the structural gaps despite rising security budgets

title: ADillesHeel: Making the Impossible Possible in AD Attack Path Analysis
speaker: Shang-De Jiang, Che Yu Lin, Cheng-Lin Yang
theme: Novel graph-simplification methodology that makes exhaustive AD attack-path enumeration tractable at enterprise scale (≥4 trillion paths in one customer environment); reveals that Tier-0 AD account counts are on average 580 % higher than organisations believe

title: Analyzing and Executing ADCS Attack Paths with BloodHound
speaker: Andy Robbins, Jonas Bülow Knudsen
theme: Debut of native ADCS attack-path support in BloodHound: live demo of discovering, executing (via Rubeus/Certify), and practically remediating ESC-class privilege-escalation paths in Microsoft's built-in PKI without business disruption

title: Attacking Primary Refresh Tokens using their macOS Implementation
speaker: Olaf Hartong, Dirk-jan Mollema
theme: First public analysis of how Microsoft implements Entra ID Primary Refresh Tokens on macOS; discovery of undocumented deviceless PRTs that can be obtained during phishing and used to bypass Conditional Access and register attacker-controlled devices — update to ROADtools released

title: Deep Dive into Windows Defender: Smart App Control and ETW
speaker: Tillmann Oßwald, Dr. Baptiste David
theme: Comprehensive reverse-engineering of Windows Defender internals — unpublished RPC interfaces, Smart App Control (WDAC-to-cloud pipeline), and ETW provider enumeration — exposing information-disclosure and tampering opportunities that EDR vendors and red teams both care about

title: Exploiting Token-Based Authentication: Attacking and Defending Identities in the 2020s
speaker: Dr Nestori Syynimaa
theme: Demo-heavy coverage of both token-replay (MITRE T1134.001) and token-forgery (T1606) across Kerberos, SAML, and OAuth against Microsoft on-prem and Entra ID — showing attacker mechanics and detection paths for each

title: Misconfiguration Manager: Overlooked and Overprivileged
speaker: Duane Michael, Chris Thompson
theme: Comprehensive attack-and-defence matrix for SCCM/MECM misconfigurations — credential access, privilege escalation, and domain compromise paths actively exploited by ransomware actors — with first SCCM Attack & Defence Matrix release

title: Resurrecting Stuxnet in 2024: Leveraging Emulated Read-Only Filesystems and NTFS Glitches for Infection and Persistence
speaker: Alessandro Magnosi
theme: Modern re-imagination of Stuxnet's attack chain exploiting unpatched NTFS implementation quirks and emulated filesystem weaknesses to deploy malicious drivers while evading HVCI/DSE; introduces "DriverJack" and new IOC patterns

title: Relay Your Heart Away: An OPSEC-Conscious Approach to 445 Takeover
speaker: Nick Powers
theme: OPSEC-aware techniques for taking control of SMB port 445 on Windows systems to enable NTLM relay attacks with reduced defensive footprint

title: Authenticating through Windows Hello for Business — a Reverse Engineering Story
speaker: Dr. Baptiste David, Tillmann Oßwald
theme: In-depth reverse engineering of Windows Hello for Business — specifically the TPM-protected biometric subsystem — showing that the integrity and confidentiality of facial-recognition biometric data can be circumvented, undermining domain authentication assurances

title: Beyond LSASS: Cutting-Edge Techniques for Undetectable Threat Emulation
speaker: Priyank Nigam
theme: Post-LSASS credential-access methods in Entra ID environments — finding and exploiting OAuth/M365 authentication tokens in memory and on disk, abusing long-lived SSO tokens and WebView2-based Chromium apps — with defender monitoring guidance

title: Breaking Boundaries: Unraveling AD Cross-Forest Attack Paths
speaker: Jonas Bülow Knudsen
theme: Systematic analysis and tooling for mapping lateral-movement paths that cross Active Directory forest trust boundaries — often invisible to single-forest tools — with BloodHound integration

title: Finding Entra ID Conditional Access Bypasses — the Structured Way
speaker: Dirk-jan Mollema, Fabian Bader
theme: Automated, at-scale analysis of hundreds of Microsoft 365 app/resource/protocol combinations to find undocumented Conditional Access policy exceptions and bypasses — including hardcoded vendor-side exceptions — that can allow MFA/compliant-device policy evasion

title: Hopping Across Devices: Expanding Lateral Movement through Pass-the-Certificate (PKU2U)
speaker: Yuya Chudo
theme: Reverse engineering of undocumented Windows PKU2U (Public Key User-to-User) P2P certificate internals to extend Pass-the-Certificate lateral movement across SMB, WinRM, and RDP to Entra-joined devices — bypassing MFA in some Conditional Access configurations. New open-source multi-protocol tool released

title: Misconfiguration Manager: Still Overlooked, Still Overprivileged
speaker: Duane Michael, Garrett Foster
theme: One year on from TR24-8: new SCCM/MECM attack primitives discovered in 2024–2025, real-world ransomware case studies, updated Attack & Defence Matrix, and an analysis of whether enterprise defenders have actually remediated what the previous talk flagged

title: RBAC: The Shady Place Behind Basic Entra ID Security
speaker: Martin Haller
theme: Demonstrates how RBAC misconfigurations across Intune, Defender, Exchange Online, Azure, Purview, and Power Platform create privilege-escalation, lateral-movement, and persistence chains that current scanning tools (PingCastle, BloodHound, ScubaGear) miss

title: Restless Guest: A Novel Entra ID Vulnerability
speaker: Simon Maxwell-Stewart
theme: First-of-its-kind research into Azure guest users being able to create and own subscriptions in external tenants without explicit privileges — a confirmed in-the-wild attack vector enabling lateral movement, backdoor identity creation, and privilege escalation that most Azure threat models do not anticipate

title: Revisiting Cross-Session Activation Attacks
speaker: Fabian Mosch
theme: Current exploitability assessment of COM Cross-Session Activation as a privilege-escalation and credential-theft vector (including post-patch analysis of certifiedDCOM, ADCSPotato, SilverPotato); new attack vectors for remote Cross-Session Activation enabling lateral movement and credential theft

title: The Crypto Game of North Korea: Stealing Money with Chrome 0-Days
speaker: Boris Larin (Kaspersky GReAT)
theme: Full-chain analysis of the May 2024 Lazarus Group campaign: a two-CVE V8-sandbox-escape chain (logic bugs only) in Chrome used against cryptocurrency targets, combined with a custom social-engineering game deployed for months on social media — critical for Windows defenders given Chrome's dominant enterprise install base

title: Demystifying Managed Service Accounts: Best Practices, Security Measures, and Windows Server 2025 dMSAs
speaker: Jorge de Almeida Pinto
theme: Security comparison of MSA → gMSA → dMSA (new in Windows Server 2025), showing migration risks, attack surface changes, and residual credential-theft paths that organisations create when adopting the newest account type incorrectly

title: TPM 2.0 Attestable Firmware: Recovering Trust after Firmware Flaws
speaker: Not listed on archive page
theme: How TPM attestation pipelines can be used to detect and recover from firmware-level compromise — directly relevant to Windows Secure Boot and device health attestation chains used by Entra ID Conditional Access

title: A New Root of Trust: Changing Computing with TEE
speaker: Not listed on archive page
theme: Examines Trusted Execution Environments (TEE) as a replacement root-of-trust — directly applicable to Microsoft Pluton, which moves the TPM security processor inside the CPU and is the foundational hardware layer for Credential Guard and VBS on new Windows 11 devices

title: Exploring Dual Edges of SRAM Data Remanence in SoCs: Covert Storage and Exfiltration Risks in TEE
speaker: Not listed on archive page
theme: SRAM data remanence in TEE-protected SoCs can be exploited for covert key exfiltration — a hardware-level threat to credentials sealed by TPM or Pluton under Windows Credential Guard/BitLocker

title: Windows 11 LPE — successful escalation to SYSTEM
speaker: DEVCORE Research Team
theme: TOCTOU race condition plus a second unspecified bug chained to achieve local privilege escalation on a fully-patched Windows 11 system

title: VMware Workstation guest-escape → SYSTEM on host Windows OS
speaker: Gwangun Jung (@pr0ln) & Junoh Lee (@bbbig12), Theori
theme: Three-bug chain — uninitialized variable + UAF + heap buffer overflow — used to escape VMware Workstation and execute code as SYSTEM on the underlying Windows host OS

title: Oracle VirtualBox guest-escape → SYSTEM on host Windows OS
speaker: Bruno PUJOS & Corentin BAYET, REverse Tactics
theme: Two Oracle VirtualBox bugs (including buffer overflow) combined with a Windows UAF to escape the guest OS and achieve SYSTEM-level code execution on the Windows host

title: Microsoft Edge + Google Chrome renderer RCE (double-tap, same bugs)
speaker: Manfred Paul (@_manfp)
theme: CWE-1284 (Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input) exploited to achieve renderer RCE on both Edge and Chrome simultaneously — notable as a single-bug cross-browser strike; Paul went on to win Master of Pwn with $202,500 total

title: Windows 11 LPE — three independent researchers succeeded on Day 2
theme: Three independent Windows 11 kernel LPE exploits landed on Day 2, all via distinct bug classes (input validation, race condition, reference count corruption) — illustrating the breadth of unpatched kernel attack surface

title: Windows 11 LPE → SYSTEM
speaker: Chen Le Qi (@cplearns2h4ck), STARLabs SG
theme: UAF chained with integer overflow to escalate privileges to SYSTEM on Windows 11

title: Windows 11 LPE → SYSTEM (type confusion)
speaker: Hyeonjin Choi (@d4m0n_8), Out Of Bounds
theme: Type confusion bug in Windows 11 kernel exploited to escalate to SYSTEM

title: Microsoft SharePoint RCE (auth bypass + insecure deserialization chain)
speaker: Dinh Ho Anh Khoa, Viettel Cyber Security
theme: Two-bug chain — authentication bypass combined with insecure deserialization — to achieve remote code execution on Microsoft SharePoint Server

title: VMware Workstation guest-escape + Windows 11 LPE → SYSTEM
speaker: Dung & Nguyen (@MochiNishimiya), STARLabs SG
theme: TOCTOU race condition used to escape VMware Workstation, then Improper Validation of Array Index leveraged to escalate privileges to SYSTEM on the Windows 11 host — full guest-to-host-SYSTEM chain

title: Windows 11 LPE → SYSTEM (race condition)
speaker: Miloš Ivanović (@ynwarcs)
theme: Race condition exploited for SYSTEM-level privilege escalation on Windows 11 — fourth-round win indicating the high volume of independent researchers holding Windows LPE bugs

title: Microsoft Edge sandbox escape (4-bug logic chain, full $175K payout)
speaker: Orange Tsai (@orange_8361), DEVCORE Research Team
theme: Four chained logic bugs in Microsoft Edge to achieve a complete sandbox escape — no memory corruption required; noteworthy for using only logic/design flaws against a mature browser sandbox

title: Windows 11 LPE → SYSTEM (Improper Access Control)
speaker: Angelboy (@scwuaptx) & TwinkleStar03 (@_twinklestar03), DEVCORE Research Team
theme: Improper access control bug in Windows 11 exploited for SYSTEM-level privilege escalation

title: Windows 11 LPE → SYSTEM (heap-based buffer overflow)
speaker: Marcin Wiążowski
theme: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows 11 kernel exploited for LPE — Wiążowski's third consecutive Pwn2Own event with a Windows 11 exploit (Vancouver 2024 × 1, Berlin 2025 × 1, Berlin 2026 × 1)

title: Windows 11 LPE → SYSTEM (2 × UAF)
speaker: Kentaro Kawane, GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae
theme: Two chained use-after-free bugs exploited for SYSTEM-level privilege escalation on Windows 11

title: Microsoft Exchange RCE as SYSTEM (3-bug chain)
speaker: Orange Tsai (@orange_8361), DEVCORE Research Team
theme: Three-bug chain to achieve remote code execution running as SYSTEM on Microsoft Exchange — maximum prize in the server category; Orange Tsai achieved both Edge sandbox escape (Day 1) and Exchange RCE (Day 2) at the same event, powering DEVCORE to Master of Pwn

title: Windows 11 LPE → SYSTEM (integer overflow)
speaker: Siyeon Wi
theme: Integer overflow exploited for Windows 11 SYSTEM-level privilege escalation

title: Microsoft SharePoint RCE (2-bug chain)
speaker: splitline (@_splitline_), DEVCORE Research Team
theme: Two-bug chain achieving remote code execution on Microsoft SharePoint Server — contributing to DEVCORE's dominant Master of Pwn finish with $505,000 and 50.5 points across the three days

title: Hot Potato — Privilege Escalation on Windows 7, 8, 10, Server 2008, Server 2012
speaker: Stephen Breen (@breenmachine) — Foxglove Security
venue: January 2016 — Foxglove Security blog post; technique developed ~2015
theme: Combines local NBNS spoofing, fake WPAD proxy, and HTTP→SMB NTLM relay to escalate to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM from any low-privilege Windows account

title: Rotten Potato — Privilege Escalation from Service Accounts to SYSTEM
speaker: Stephen Breen (@breenmachine) + Chris Mallz (@vvalien1) — Foxglove Security
venue: September 2016 — DerbyCon VI; blog post 26 September 2016
theme: Tricks DCOM/COM's CoGetInstanceFromIStorage to coerce NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM to authenticate via NTLM to port 6666, then relays and locally impersonates the resulting token

title: Juicy Potato (abusing the golden privileges)
speaker: Andrea Pierini (@decoder_it) + Giuseppe Trotta (@Giutro) — independent researchers / OHPE
theme: Extends RottenPotato to any DCOM COM server that implements IMarshal and runs as an elevated user, allowing custom CLSID selection and custom COM listening port

title: RoguePotato
speaker: Antonio Cocomazzi (@splinter_code) + Andrea Pierini (@decoder_it)
venue: April 2020 — GitHub release; preceded by blog post "We thought they were potatoes but they were beans" (December 2019)
theme: Works around Microsoft's post-1809 OXID resolver port-135 restriction by redirecting COM activation traffic through a remote forwarder to a local fake OXID resolver, recovering a SYSTEM impersonation token

title: PrintSpoofer — Abusing Impersonate Privileges on Windows 10 and Server 2019
speaker: Clément Labro (@itm4n) — independent researcher
theme: Uses the Windows Print Spooler's RpcRemoteFindFirstPrinterChangeNotification call to coerce SYSTEM to connect to a named pipe, then calls ImpersonateNamedPipeClient() to steal the token — no COM/DCOM needed

title: Sharing a Logon Session a Little Too Much
speaker: James Forshaw (@tiraniddo) — Google Project Zero
theme: Demonstrates that the first NETWORK SERVICE logon session token (owned by RPCSS) is reused for all loopback SMB named-pipe authentications, allowing any NETWORK SERVICE process to impersonate RPCSS and gain AllAccess to higher-privileged service processes

title: Evil Printer: How to Hack Windows Machines with Printer Protocols
speaker: Zhipeng Huo (@R3dF09) + Yunhai Zhang (@cloudnine_sec) — Tencent Security Xuanwu Lab
theme: Surveys MS-RPRN, MS-PAR, and related printer RPC interfaces as coercion primitives to force domain controllers to authenticate outbound, enabling NTLM relay and credential theft

title: PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675 / CVE-2021-34527)
speaker: Original CVE-2021-1675 PoC: Zhiniang Peng (@edwardzpeng) + Xuefeng Li (@lxf02942370) — Sangfor Technologies; expanded CVE-2021-34527 analysis and public RCE: Benjamin Delpy, Cube0x0, multiple researchers
venue: June–July 2021 — GitHub PoC release, then Microsoft emergency advisory
theme: Exploits the Windows Print Spooler's RpcAddPrinterDriverEx() to load arbitrary DLLs as SYSTEM from a remote SMB share, enabling unauthenticated RCE / LPE on all unpatched Windows versions

title: PetitPotam — Unauthenticated NTLM Relay Against Active Directory Certificate Services
speaker: Lionel Gilles (@topotam77) — independent researcher
theme: Abuses MS-EFSRPC's EfsRpcOpenFileRaw (accessible unauthenticated via LSARPC named pipe) to coerce any Windows machine including domain controllers to authenticate outbound to an attacker-controlled server, enabling relay to AD CS web enrollment for domain-level certificate theft

title: Certified Pre-Owned: Abusing Active Directory Certificate Services
speaker: Will Schroeder (@harmj0y) + Lee Christensen (@tifkin_) — SpecterOps

title: Zerologon: Unauthenticated Domain Controller Compromise by Subverting Netlogon Cryptography
speaker: Tom Tervoort (Senior Security Specialist) — Secura (Bureau Veritas Cybersecurity)
venue: September 2020 — Secura whitepaper; CVE patched August 2020 Patch Tuesday
theme: Exploits a cryptographic flaw in the Netlogon Remote Protocol's AES-CFB8 authentication scheme — an all-zero IV allows brute-forcing the session key in ~256 attempts — to reset the domain controller machine account password to a known value without any prior credentials

title: Six Degrees of Domain Admin

title: Mimikatz Golden Ticket & the Evolution of Kerberos Attacks in Active Directory
speaker: Sean Metcalf (@PyroTek3) — TrimarcSecurity / ADSecurity.org; derived from Benjamin Delpy's (@gentilkiwi) Mimikatz implementation
venue: 2014–2015 — ADSecurity.org blog series; Black Hat USA 2015 talk "Red vs Blue: Modern Active Directory Attacks, Detection and Protection"
theme: Documents how possession of the KRBTGT account hash allows forging arbitrary Kerberos TGTs (Golden Tickets) that are accepted without contacting the DC, enabling indefinite stealthy domain persistence

title: Mimikatz: Post-Exploitation Credential Extraction and Kerberos Manipulation
speaker: Benjamin Delpy (@gentilkiwi) — independent researcher
venue: 2011 (initial release); Microsoft BlueHat 2014 presentation; actively maintained through 2023
theme: Extracts plaintext passwords, NTLM hashes, and Kerberos tickets directly from Windows LSASS memory and implements Pass-the-Hash, Pass-the-Ticket, and Kerberos ticket forgery

title: The original NTLM Pass-the-Hash attack; later operationalised in the "Pass-The-Hash Toolkit"

venue: 1997 — Samba mailing list; 2008 — Black Hat DC (Ochoa toolkit)
theme: NT/LAN Manager authentication can be satisfied by sending a captured NTLM hash directly — without knowing the cleartext password — enabling lateral movement across Windows networks

title: Attacking Kerberos: Kicking the Guard Dog of Hades
speaker: Tim Medin (@timmedin) — Red Siege Information Security
theme: Any authenticated domain user can request a TGS service ticket for any SPN-registered account and take it offline for password cracking, since the ticket is encrypted with the service account's NTLM hash

title: MS14-068: Vulnerability in Kerberos Could Allow Elevation of Privilege
speaker: Originally discovered by researchers (credited to Tom Maddock / NSA attribution debated); public PoC by Sylvain Monné (@skipfish) and subsequently by Nikhil Mittal (@nikhil_mitt) "Kekeo" / PyKEK
venue: November 2014 — Microsoft Security Bulletin; public PoC within weeks
theme: A validation flaw in the Kerberos KDC allows any domain user to forge a PAC with arbitrary group memberships (including Domain Admins), granting full DA rights on any unpatched DC

title: Empire: A PowerShell Post-Exploitation Framework
speaker: Will Schroeder (@harmj0y), Justin Warner (@sixdub), Matt Nelson (@enigma0x3), rvrsh3ll, killswitch_gui, xorrior — SpecterOps (then independent)
theme: A Python/PowerShell2 post-exploitation C2 framework that runs PowerShell agents without powershell.exe, implements in-memory module loading, encrypted comms, and 300+ post-exploitation modules

title: Rubeus
speaker: Will Schroeder (@harmj0y) — SpecterOps; co-contributors Charlie Clark (@exploitph), Ceri Coburn (@_EthicalChaos_), Elad Shamir
theme: A C# toolset for raw Kerberos ticket requests, renewals, Kerberoasting, AS-REP roasting, Pass-the-Ticket, ticket forgery (Golden/Silver/Diamond), and PKINIT operations — all without touching lsass.exe

title: SharpDPAPI
speaker: Will Schroeder (@harmj0y) — SpecterOps (port of Benjamin Delpy's Mimikatz DPAPI logic)
theme: Extracts and decrypts DPAPI master keys, Windows Credential Manager secrets, RDP passwords, Chrome/Edge browser credentials, and certificate private keys without requiring SYSTEM privileges

title: noPAC — CVE-2021-42287 / CVE-2021-42278 (Sam-Account-Name Spoofing)
speaker: Charlie Clark (@exploitph) — SpecterOps; detailed by Andrew Bartlett (Samba), public PoC by Cube0x0 and WazeHell
venue: November 2021 — Patch Tuesday; public PoC December 2021
theme: Any low-privileged domain user can rename their machine account to impersonate the DC's short name, request a TGT, then restore the name — the KDC appends "$" to the original DC account, yielding a DC-level PAC without needing its hash

title: Windows: DCOM DCE/RPC Local NTLM Reflection Elevation of Privilege
speaker: James Forshaw (@tiraniddo) — Google Project Zero
theme: The COM CoGetInstanceFromIStorage API can be abused to coerce the local SYSTEM account to perform NTLM authentication to an attacker-controlled RPC endpoint, and the resulting NTLM exchange can be relayed back to obtain a SYSTEM-level impersonation token

title: Windows 10(HH) Symbolic Link Mitigations
speaker: James Forshaw (@tiraniddo) — Google Project Zero
theme: Documents how Windows 10 and back-ported MS15-090 restrict low-privileged creation of Object Manager symbolic links and NTFS mount points, explaining why these primitives were previously so powerful for EoP and how the new restrictions work

title: Bochspwn: Identifying 0-days via system-wide memory access pattern analysis
speaker: Mateusz 'j00ru' Jurczyk + Gynvael Coldwind — Google
venue: August 2013 — Black Hat USA 2013 (original); August 2017 — Black Hat USA 2017 (Reloaded)
theme: Uses Bochs x86 full-system emulation to instrument every memory access in a running OS, automatically detecting double-fetches (race conditions) and uninitialized memory disclosures in the Windows/Linux kernel

title: Windows Notification Facility: Useless or Useful? (blog series)
speaker: James Forshaw (@tiraniddo) — Google Project Zero
theme: Reverse-engineers the undocumented Windows Notification Facility (WNF), a kernel-level publish-subscribe mechanism, revealing that WNF state data is accessible from user-mode and provides novel attack primitives for cross-process information leakage and sandbox escape

title: Reading Privileged Memory with a Side-Channel (Spectre/Meltdown)

theme: CPU speculative execution and data-cache timing can be used to read arbitrary kernel and hypervisor memory from unprivileged user-mode code, breaking all OS and hypervisor memory isolation assumptions
